requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | all timer ) "." stop
requirements.canonical: The stop timer operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | all timer ) "." stop.

examples.text:
t_myTimer1.stop;  // stops t_myTimer1 
  all timer.stop;  // stops all running timers

requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.3 -- ( ObjectReference | all timer ) "." stop

requirements.original: A stop operation removes a running timer from the list of running timers.
requirements.canonical: A timer stopped by the stop timer operation IS removed from the running-timer list.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.3 -- A stop operation removes a running timer from the list of running timers.

requirements.original: A stopped timer becomes inactive and its elapsed time is set to the float value zero (0.0).
requirements.canonical: A stopped timer IS inactive.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.3 -- A stopped timer becomes inactive and its elapsed time is set to the float value zero (0.0).

requirements.original: A stopped timer becomes inactive and its elapsed time is set to the float value zero (0.0).
requirements.canonical: The elapsed time of a stopped timer IS set to the float value 0.0.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.3 -- A stopped timer becomes inactive and its elapsed time is set to the float value zero (0.0).

requirements.original: Stopping an inactive timer is a valid operation, although it does not have any effect.
requirements.canonical: Stopping an inactive timer IS a valid operation without any effect.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.3 -- Stopping an inactive timer is a valid operation, although it does not have any effect.

requirements.original: Stopping an expired timer causes the entry for this timer in the timeout-list to be removed.
requirements.canonical: When an expired timer is stopped, the entry for the timer IS removed from the timeout-list.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.3 -- Stopping an expired timer causes the entry for this timer in the timeout-list to be removed.

requirements.original: The all keyword may be used to stop all timers that have been started on a test component or control component.
requirements.canonical: The `all` keyword MAY be used with the stop timer operation (`all timer.stop`) to stop all timers started on a test component or control component.

examples.text:
t_myTimer1.stop;  // stops t_myTimer1 
  all timer.stop;  // stops all running timers

requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.3 -- The all keyword may be used to stop all timers that have been started on a test component or control component.

requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of the timer type.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a stop timer operation SHALL be of the timer type.

examples.text:
t_myTimer1.stop;  // stops t_myTimer1 
  all timer.stop;  // stops all running timers

requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.3 -- a) The ObjectReference shall be of the timer type.

requirements.original: ObjectReference "." read
requirements.canonical: The read timer operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." read.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.4 -- ObjectReference "." read

requirements.original: The read operation returns the time that has elapsed since the specified timer was started.
requirements.canonical: The result of the read timer operation IS the time elapsed since the specified timer was started.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.4 -- The read operation returns the time that has elapsed since the specified timer was started.

requirements.original: The returned value shall be of type float.
requirements.canonical: The value returned by the read timer operation SHALL be of type float.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.4 -- The returned value shall be of type float.

requirements.original: Applying the read operation on an inactive timer, i.e. on a timer not listed on the running-timer list, will return the float value zero (0.0).
requirements.canonical: When applied to an inactive timer (a timer not in the running-timer list), the result of the read timer operation IS the float value 0.0.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.4 -- Applying the read operation on an inactive timer, i.e. on a timer not listed on the running-timer list, will return the float value zero (0.0).

requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of the timer type.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a read timer operation SHALL be of the timer type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.4 -- a) The ObjectReference shall be of the timer type.

requirements.original: ( ObjectReference ) | any timer | any from TimerArrayRef ) "." running ["->" @index value ValueRef]
requirements.canonical: The running timer operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | any timer | any from TimerArrayRef ) "." running [ "->" @index value ValueRef ].

ambiguity.issue: the syntax block in the standard has an unbalanced parenthesis after ObjectReference

examples.text: if (t_myTimer1.running) { … }
if (any timer.running) { … }

requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- ( ObjectReference ) | any timer | any from TimerArrayRef ) "." running ["->" @index value ValueRef]

requirements.original: The running timer operation is used to check whether a specific timer visible in the given scope unit is listed on the running-timer list or not (i.e. that it has been started and has neither timed out nor been stopped).
requirements.canonical: The running timer operation IS checking whether a specific timer visible in the scope unit is in the running-timer list, i.e. has been started and has neither timed out nor been stopped.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- The running timer operation is used to check whether a specific timer visible in the given scope unit is listed on the running-timer list or not (i.e. that it has been started and has neither timed out nor been stopped).

requirements.original: The operation returns the value true if the timer is listed on the list, false otherwise.
requirements.canonical: The running timer operation IS returning `true` if the timer is in the running-timer list and `false` otherwise.

examples.text: if (t_myTimer1.running) { … }

requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- The operation returns the value true if the timer is listed on the list, false otherwise.

requirements.original: The any keyword may be used to check if any timer started on a test component or control component is running.
requirements.canonical: The `any` keyword MAY be used with the running timer operation (`any timer.running`) to check whether any timer started on a test component or control component is running.

examples.text: if (any timer.running) { … }

requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- The any keyword may be used to check if any timer started on a test component or control component is running.

requirements.original: When the any from `TimerArrayRef` notation is used, where TimerArrayRef shall be a timer array identifier, the timers from the referenced array are iterated over and their states are checked individually, from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.
requirements.canonical: The TimerArrayRef in an `any from` running timer operation SHALL be a timer array identifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- When the any from `TimerArrayRef` notation is used, where TimerArrayRef shall be a timer array identifier, the timers from the referenced array are iterated over and their states are checked individually, from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.

requirements.original: When the any from `TimerArrayRef` notation is used, where TimerArrayRef shall be a timer array identifier, the timers from the referenced array are iterated over and their states are checked individually, from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.
requirements.canonical: In an `any from` running timer operation, the timers of the referenced timer array ARE checked individually, iterating from the innermost to the outermost dimension and from the lowest to the highest index in each dimension.

ambiguity.issue: 'from innermost to outermost dimension' does not state clearly which index varies fastest.
readings: The index of the innermost (last) dimension varies fastest, i.e. row-major order [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
The innermost dimension is processed first as the slowest-varying index.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- When the any from `TimerArrayRef` notation is used, where TimerArrayRef shall be a timer array identifier, the timers from the referenced array are iterated over and their states are checked individually, from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.

requirements.original: The first timer to be found in the running state causes the operation returning with the true value.
requirements.canonical: When a timer of the timer array is found in the running state, the result of an `any from` running timer operation IS `true` and the iteration stops.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- The first timer to be found in the running state causes the operation returning with the true value.

requirements.original: If no running timer is found in the array, the operation returns with the false value.
requirements.canonical: If no timer of the timer array is running, the result of an `any from` running timer operation IS `false`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- If no running timer is found in the array, the operation returns with the false value.

requirements.original: The index of the first timer found running can optionally be stored in an integer variable for a single-dimensional array, or to an integer array or record of integer variable for multi-dimensional timer arrays.
requirements.canonical: The index of the first running timer found by an `any from` running timer operation MAY be stored via index redirection in an integer variable for a single-dimensional timer array, or in an integer array or record of integer variable for a multi-dimensional timer array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- The index of the first timer found running can optionally be stored in an integer variable for a single-dimensional array, or to an integer array or record of integer variable for multi-dimensional timer arrays.

requirements.original: a) TimerArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized timer array.
requirements.canonical: The TimerArrayRef of an `any from` running timer operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized timer array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- a) TimerArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized timer array.

requirements.original: b) The index redirection shall only be used for any from timer array running operations.
requirements.canonical: The index redirection in a running timer operation SHALL only be used with an `any from` timer array running operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- b) The index redirection shall only be used for any from timer array running operations.

requirements.original: c) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional timer arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective timer array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection of a running timer operation is used for a single-dimensional timer array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the timer array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- c) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional timer arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective timer array.

requirements.original: d) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional timer arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective timer array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the timer array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection of a running timer operation is used for a multi-dimensional timer array, the size of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL be exactly the number of dimensions of the timer array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- d) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional timer arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective timer array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the timer array.

requirements.original: d) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional timer arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective timer array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the timer array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection of a running timer operation is used for a multi-dimensional timer array, the element type of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the timer array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- d) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional timer arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective timer array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the timer array.

requirements.original: e) The ObjectReference shall be of the timer type.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a running timer operation SHALL be of the timer type.

examples.text: if (t_myTimer1.running) { … }

requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.5 -- e) The ObjectReference shall be of the timer type.

requirements.original: [ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any timer | any from TimerArrayRef ) "." timeout ["->" @index value ValueRef]
requirements.canonical: The timeout operation has the syntax [ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any timer | any from TimerArrayRef ) "." timeout [ "->" @index value ValueRef ].

examples.text: t_myTimer1.timeout; // checks for the timeout of the previously started timer MyTimer1
any timer.timeout; // checks for the timeout of any previously started timer

requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- [ @nodefault ] ( ObjectReference | any timer | any from TimerArrayRef ) "." timeout ["->" @index value ValueRef]

requirements.original: The timeout operation allows to check the expiration of a specific timer in the scope unit of a test component or control component in which the timeout operation has been called or of any timer that has been started on a test component or control component before entering the scope in which the timeout operation has been called.
requirements.canonical: The timeout operation IS checking the expiration of a specific timer of the scope unit in which it is called, or of any timer started on the test component or control component before entering that scope.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence lists two alternatives without stating which syntax form addresses which; it is unclear whether 'any timer' also covers timers that are not visible in the scope.
readings: `T.timeout` checks a timer visible in the scope unit, and `any timer.timeout` checks any timer started on the component, including timers not visible in the scope.
Both forms only check timers visible in the scope unit in which the timeout operation is called.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- The timeout operation allows to check the expiration of a specific timer in the scope unit of a test component or control component in which the timeout operation has been called or of any timer that has been started on a test component or control component before entering the scope in which the timeout operation has been called.

requirements.original: When a timeout operation is processed, if a timer name is indicated, the timeout-list is searched according to the TTCN-3 scope rules.
requirements.canonical: When a timeout operation with a timer name is processed, the timeout-list IS searched according to the TTCN-3 scope rules.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- When a timeout operation is processed, if a timer name is indicated, the timeout-list is searched according to the TTCN-3 scope rules.

requirements.original: If there is a timeout event matching the timer name, that event is removed from the timeout-list, and the timeout operation succeeds.
requirements.canonical: If the timeout-list contains a timeout event matching the timer name, the event IS removed from the timeout-list and the timeout operation succeeds.
requirements.condition: a matching timeout event is in the timeout-list

examples.text: t_myTimer1.timeout; // checks for the timeout of the previously started timer MyTimer1

requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- If there is a timeout event matching the timer name, that event is removed from the timeout-list, and the timeout operation succeeds.

requirements.original: The timeout can be used to determine an alternative in an alt statement or as stand-alone statement in a behaviour description.
requirements.canonical: The timeout operation MAY be used as an alternative of an alt statement or as a stand-alone statement in a behaviour description.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- The timeout can be used to determine an alternative in an alt statement or as stand-alone statement in a behaviour description.

requirements.original: In the latter case a timeout operation is considered to be shorthand for an alt statement with the timeout operation as the only alternative.
requirements.canonical: A stand-alone timeout operation IS shorthand for an alt statement with the timeout operation as its only alternative.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- In the latter case a timeout operation is considered to be shorthand for an alt statement with the timeout operation as the only alternative.

requirements.original: If the @nodefault modifier is placed before a stand-alone timeout operation, the implicit alt statement also contains the @nodefault modifier.
requirements.canonical: If the `@nodefault` modifier is placed before a stand-alone timeout operation, the implicit alt statement IS an alt statement with the `@nodefault` modifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- If the @nodefault modifier is placed before a stand-alone timeout operation, the implicit alt statement also contains the @nodefault modifier.

requirements.original: The any keyword used with the timeout operation succeeds if the timeout-list is not empty.
requirements.canonical: A timeout operation with the `any` keyword (`any timer.timeout`) IS successful if the timeout-list is not empty.

examples.text: any timer.timeout; // checks for the timeout of any previously started timer

requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- The any keyword used with the timeout operation succeeds if the timeout-list is not empty.

requirements.original: When the any from `TimerArrayRef` notation is used, where TimerArrayRef shall be a timer array identifier, the timers from the referenced array are iterated over and individually checked for timeout from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.
requirements.canonical: The TimerArrayRef in an `any from` timeout operation SHALL be a timer array identifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- When the any from `TimerArrayRef` notation is used, where TimerArrayRef shall be a timer array identifier, the timers from the referenced array are iterated over and individually checked for timeout from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.

requirements.original: When the any from `TimerArrayRef` notation is used, where TimerArrayRef shall be a timer array identifier, the timers from the referenced array are iterated over and individually checked for timeout from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.
requirements.canonical: In an `any from` timeout operation, the timers of the referenced timer array ARE checked individually for timeout, iterating from the innermost to the outermost dimension and from the lowest to the highest index in each dimension.

ambiguity.issue: 'from innermost to outermost dimension' does not state clearly which index varies fastest.
readings: The index of the innermost (last) dimension varies fastest, i.e. row-major order.
The innermost dimension is processed first as the slowest-varying index.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- When the any from `TimerArrayRef` notation is used, where TimerArrayRef shall be a timer array identifier, the timers from the referenced array are iterated over and individually checked for timeout from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.

requirements.original: The first timer to be found in the timeout-list causes that timer to be removed from the list and the timeout operation succeeds.
requirements.canonical: In an `any from` timeout operation, the first timer of the array found in the timeout-list IS removed from the timeout-list and the timeout operation succeeds.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- The first timer to be found in the timeout-list causes that timer to be removed from the list and the timeout operation succeeds.

requirements.original: The index of the matched timer can be optionally stored in an integer variable for single-dimensional arrays or to an integer array or record of integer variable for multi-dimensional timer arrays.
requirements.canonical: The index of the matched timer of an `any from` timeout operation MAY be stored via index redirection in an integer variable for a single-dimensional timer array, or in an integer array or record of integer variable for a multi-dimensional timer array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- The index of the matched timer can be optionally stored in an integer variable for single-dimensional arrays or to an integer array or record of integer variable for multi-dimensional timer arrays.

requirements.original: a) The timeout operation does not return any value and therefore shall not be used in an expression.
requirements.canonical: The timeout operation SHALL NOT be used in an expression.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- a) The timeout operation does not return any value and therefore shall not be used in an expression.

requirements.original: b) TimerArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized timer array.
requirements.canonical: The TimerArrayRef of an `any from` timeout operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized timer array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- b) TimerArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized timer array.

requirements.original: c) The index redirection shall only be used for any from timer array timeout operations.
requirements.canonical: The index redirection in a timeout operation SHALL only be used with an `any from` timer array timeout operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- c) The index redirection shall only be used for any from timer array timeout operations.

requirements.original: d) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional timer arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective timer array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection of a timeout operation is used for a single-dimensional timer array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the timer array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- d) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional timer arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective timer array.

requirements.original: e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional timer arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective timer array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the timer array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection of a timeout operation is used for a multi-dimensional timer array, the size of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL be exactly the number of dimensions of the timer array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional timer arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective timer array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the timer array.

requirements.original: e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional timer arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective timer array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the timer array.
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection of a timeout operation is used for a multi-dimensional timer array, the element type of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the timer array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional timer arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective timer array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the timer array.

requirements.original: f) The ObjectReference shall be of the timer type.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a timeout operation SHALL be of the timer type.

examples.text: t_myTimer1.timeout; // checks for the timeout of the previously started timer MyTimer1

requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- f) The ObjectReference shall be of the timer type.

requirements.original: g) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone timeout statements.
requirements.canonical: The `@nodefault` modifier SHALL only be used in a stand-alone timeout statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 23.6 -- g) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone timeout statements.
